guarantees.claim: When EnMasking is true, zero_with_endbit[0] is driven to all zeros.
When EnMasking is true, zero_with_endbit[1][MsgWidth-1] is driven to end_of_block, and bits [MsgWidth-2:0] are driven to zero.
When EnMasking is false, zero_with_endbit[0][MsgWidth-1] is driven to end_of_block, and bits [MsgWidth-2:0] are driven to zero.
keccak_addr_o is driven to sent_message when sent_message < block_addr_limit, else to '0.

assumptions.claim: Parameter MsgWidth must be at least 2; otherwise the part-select [MsgWidth-2:0] becomes illegal when MsgWidth=1.
assumptions.cond: any use of MsgWidth in part-selects
assumptions.risk: Compilation error or simulation X-propagation if MsgWidth=1 is used.

assumptions.claim: Signal end_of_block is expected to be a single-bit value, as it is assigned to a scalar bit position.
assumptions.cond: end_of_block is used as a 1-bit assignment
assumptions.risk: If end_of_block is wider than 1 bit, the assignment may truncate and cause a mismatch with designer intent.

uncertain_points.claim: In the unmasked case (EnMasking=0), zero_with_endbit[1] is not assigned. If zero_with_endbit[1] is read elsewhere, this missing driver will cause X-propagation or unintended behavior. It is unclear whether this is intentional or a bug.
uncertain_points.cond: EnMasking == 0, and zero_with_endbit[1] is used in downstream logic
uncertain_points.risk: Potential X-propagation leading to functional failure or security vulnerability if zero_with_endbit is part of a masking scheme.

uncertain_points.claim: The generate block does not protect against MsgWidth=1. Under both EnMasking true and false branches, the part-select [MsgWidth-2:0] would be [-1:0], which is illegal in SystemVerilog, causing a compile error.
uncertain_points.risk: Design becomes unsynthesizable; if not caught, the IP may fail integration.
